$comment: Upward-import allowlist for docs-internal/ENGINE_MIGRATION_PLAN.md Arc 0. Each row is a module importing a HIGHER layer than itself — known debt that Arcs 1-4 unwind. The list ratchets DOWN only: a new edge, a grown edge, and a stale row all fail scripts/check-layering.cjs. Regenerate with `npm run check:layering:update` and give every new row a real reason.

commands -> validation.reason: process-partials.ts calls the partial-template validator, formatter and its types. Arc 3: when the command gets a compile(), the validator arrives by injection instead of by import.

expressions -> performance.reason: logical/index.ts imports matchesWithCache. Arc 7 makes per-evaluation caching and tracking an opt-in devtools wrapper rather than a hot-path dependency.

expressions -> validation.reason: base-expression / logical / special import the lightweight-validators zod clone for their `inputSchema` fields. Arc 7 deletes those fields (nothing reads them at runtime); the clone itself goes in Arc 6a.

parser -> commands.reason: TWO different problems sharing an edge. parser-constants.ts -> commands/manifest is DELIBERATE (Arc A's derive-don't-trust: the COMMANDS set is seeded from the manifest, not re-typed) and inverts in Arc 3, when a command registers its own grammar. parser/runtime.ts -> commands/helpers/{variable-access,target-elements} is the evaluator reaching sideways, and leaves with the file — see `parser -> expressions`.

parser -> compatibility.reason: parser/regex-parser.ts imports the lite BUNDLE it is meant to be a component of, inverting the whole stack in one line. Arc 5 (parser tiers) is where this is repaired; until then it is the single most backwards edge in the graph.

parser -> expressions.reason: All five are parser/runtime.ts, which is not a parser: it is the 1,967-line canonical EVALUATOR, filed under parser/ for historical reasons. Relocating that one file to the runtime layer removes these five AND two of the three `parser -> commands` imports — 7 of the 22 value edges in this file. Arc 2 types it; Arc 4 moves it. Arc 7 step 3 (2026-09-04) added two: parser/runtime.ts references `referencesExpressions` and `logicalExpressions` statically instead of looking 23 core-set names up on the context's registry — the direction step 4 wants (semantics beside the evaluator), on an edge that leaves when this file moves to runtime/.

root:metadata -> commands.reason: metadata.ts reads COMMAND_NAMES from the data-only manifest so packageInfo.commands is derived rather than hand-typed (Arc A step 4.4 — the hand-typed version had rotted three minors). Deliberate and worth keeping; resolvable later by placing the data-only manifest at layer 0, which is what it already is in spirit.

runtime -> registry.reason: runtime-base.ts imports RegistryIntegration for enhanceContext — the Proxy that wraps every handler context. Arc 4c deletes it (measured 2026-08-30: no package outside src/registry/ registers a context provider).

types -> behaviors.reason: types/index.ts re-exports behavior config types. Type-only, so it erases at build time and creates no runtime cycle; it is barrel convenience, not coupling.

types -> commands.reason: types/index.ts re-exports three command input types (swap, push-url, replace-url). Type-only. Arc 3 gives these a home in the per-command node types, and the barrel rows go with them.

types -> core.reason: base-types.ts imports the ExpressionRegistry TYPE for ExecutionContext.registry. Type-only, and it disappears in Arc 7 when the registry becomes Pratt-table entries.

types -> validation.reason: The zod clone. Ten imports across seven type modules, four of them VALUE imports of `v`/`z` for schemas that types/context-types.ts already documents as any-typed and unused. Arc 6a deletes the schemas; the clone itself has no other consumer once features/ and context/ go.
